coachingPoints: Stay low — the taller you get during the move, the slower and more exposed the dribble becomes.
Eyes up, always. If you stare at the ball between your legs, a help defender will arrive unnoticed.
The bounce should pass under your forward leg, roughly below your knee.
Protect the ball with your body: your torso should block the defender's reach on the switch.
Drill it moving before stationary — this move is designed for full-speed use.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the ball too far in front of the body — fix: the bounce point belongs directly under or slightly behind your forward leg.
Looking down at the legs — fix: pick a wall target and dribble with eyes on it, slowing down until the feel is natural.
Standing tall during the move — fix: exaggerate the knee bend; your head should drop at least 6 inches as you begin.
Swinging the ball too wide through the legs — fix: aim for a tight, compact pass of the ball from front hand to back hand.
description: Bounce the ball through your legs to switch hands while keeping the ball shielded — perfect for tight spaces and full-speed moves.
gameSituations: Pushing the ball in transition — a between-the-legs switch lets you change hands at full speed without breaking stride.
Beating a defender who is crowding you — the move keeps the ball behind your body, where his reach cannot follow.
Changing direction on a drive — when the lane closes on your strong side, switch hands through the legs and attack the new gap.

howTo.detail: Start in a low stance, dribbling with your right hand. Push the ball forward slightly and step forward with your left leg, opening a gap to bounce through.
howTo.title: Dribble and step forward

howTo.detail: Aim the bounce at the floor under your forward (left) leg — between knee and foot. A lower, shorter bounce is easier to control than a high one.
howTo.title: Bounce under your lead leg

howTo.detail: As the ball pops up behind you, catch it with your left hand. Your right hand releases the moment the ball clears your leg.
howTo.title: Catch with the opposite hand

howTo.detail: The instant your left hand secures the ball, take a hard dribble and explode — change direction or speed, never just keep gliding.
howTo.title: Push off and accelerate

howTo.detail: Work from stationary → walking → jogging → full speed. At each speed, do 10 clean reps per side before moving up.
howTo.title: Build speed gradually

title: Between the Legs
whatIsIt: Between the legs is a ball-handling move where you bounce the ball through the space under your forward leg, switching it from one hand to the other. The dribble travels from the front of your body to behind your stance, which makes it naturally protected from defenders.

Unlike a crossover, which moves the ball across your front, between the legs keeps the ball behind your legs and under your body. That is why advanced guards use it at full speed in transition: it is one of the safest ways to switch hands while moving.
whyItMatters: When you are sprinting down the court, switching hands in front of your body invites a defender to poke the ball free. Between the legs keeps the ball shielded the entire time, so it is the go-to move for guards who attack at speed. It also opens up combos — between the legs into a crossover, a step-back, or a hesitation — because the ball ends up safely in your other hand.
